planned_outcome: Land HMS Daring: reformulate Luikov-tin with observed T_air(t) and h_eff(t) extracted from sensors (replacing fitted T_oven_eff and Bi_top); add oven-spring alpha(T) piecewise profile (alpha_post/alpha_pre as free parameter or pinned at 0.4); per-fixture diagnostics for steam phase and oven spring window; reduced free parameters from M15's 8 down to 4-5.
actual_outcome: Reformulated Luikov-tin with observed T_air(t) and h_eff(t) inputs plus oven-spring alpha(T) profile. Phase 1 diagnostic: 0/7 fixtures had steam (consistent with lab/single-zone bakes); oven-spring window detected 9-15 min into bake on all 7. Phase 2 forward sanity 8/8 PASS. Phase 3 synthetic recovery: 3/3 seeds with all 5 params interior, RMSE 0.55 deg C — formulation IS identifiable on Zurcher-class data. BUT Phase 4 real-CSV: median main-bake RMSE 37.3 deg C — WORSE than M15's 6.1 and M9's 5-11. Diagnosis: the M2a-flagged ambient sensor reads the air-NEAR-loaf (cooled by evaporative effects) not the bulk oven air. Using it as the radiative-convective BC source feeds the wrong driving temperature; the optimizer has no good knobs to compensate. M9's approach (Dirichlet using interpolated T_surface) is empirically the best BC formulation we've found. CONFIRM-information-limit: 13 inverse-problem missions now confirm the ~6 deg C floor is structural; no model class or BC formulation breaks below it. Method 1 + Method 4 stub is the unambiguous production path.
success_metric_result: 8/8 forward sanity tests PASS; synthetic recovery 3/3 within 30%; real-CSV 5/7 converged but median RMSE 37.3 deg C; LOO T1 RMSE 46.7 deg C; observed-BC reformulation regressed vs M15 because ambient sensor measures local air (cooled by evaporation) not bulk oven.

adopt: M2a 'ambient' sensors measure the air NEAR THE LOAF in the boundary layer, NOT bulk oven air. Use them with caution as BC sources
Observed-BC reformulation can REGRESS results when the observable doesn't match the modelled physical quantity
avoid: Treating M2a's 'ambient' classification as equivalent to 'bulk oven temperature'; the boundary layer matters
